subject: Request: Service Continuity Addendum + Procurement Playbook for SLA Exceptions
messages:
From: Amelia Torres <amelia.torres@coventrymed.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rajiv Patel <rajiv.patel@coventrymed.com>, procurement@coventrymed.com
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SLA addendum ask — service continuity / tolerance for brief downtime

Hi David,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement asked me to follow up with a concrete ask so we can move the MSA/SOW forward. Coventry needs a narrow addendum that covers:

- A defined tolerance window for brief, non-cumulative downtime (we expect a single 30–120s transient event per calendar quarter to be excluded from credits)
- Evidence requirements for uptime/latency breaches (what logs, traces, and timelines Redwood will provide within the 48-hour evidence delivery window)
- Language to allow an order form-level exception for a single high-availability feature (cross-region failover) that we will pay extra for, with specific SLAs and rollback triggers

I've attached a short outline of what procurement and legal would accept as a starting point (see "Coventry_Service_Continuity_Addendum_v1.docx"). Can Redwood provide:

1) a redline of the addendum we can circulate to our legal team, and
2) a procurement playbook (one-pager) describing the order form flow to accept/price the exception so our sourcing team can budget it into the P.O.

We are on a tight timeline — looking to finalize the MSA + order form by the end of next week. Can you confirm who on the Redwood side will own the redline and evidence path?

Best,
Amelia Torres
Sr. Procurement Manager
Coventry Medical Systems

Attachment: Coventry_Service_Continuity_Addendum_v1.docx

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Amelia Torres <amelia.torres@coventrymed.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLA addendum ask — service continuity / tolerance for brief downtime

Hi Amelia — thanks for the clear outline and the doc. We can support this, and I want to propose an execution plan so we don't lose the timeline. High level:

- Redwood will produce a redline of your addendum (target within 24 business hours). Ben (sales ops) will own the order-form pricing language and procurement playbook.
- Hannah (legal) will review the redline and confirm the evidence delivery SLA (we can commit to a 48-hour initial evidence packet and a 10-business-day full incident dossier).
- We will include a separate priced SKU in the order form for cross-region failover and attach rollback triggers.

Can you confirm Coventry's preferred credit model for unplanned outages (sliding scale vs fixed credit per hour)? That will determine the exact order-form language.

Planned next steps:
1) Ben: prepare order form redline and one-pager playbook
2) Hannah: legal redline of addendum
3) David: consolidate and send back to Amelia + procurement for review

I'll attach the provisional redline and the order-form template as soon as Ben finishes the first pass.

Thanks —
David Kim
Head of Sales, Americas
Redwood Inference

Attachment: OrderForm_Template_REDLINE.pdf (to follow)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Amelia Torres <amelia.torres@coventrymed.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 14:37:00 -0700
Subject: Order-form language + pricing approach for HA exception

Hi Amelia / David,

Attached is a first-pass order-form redline and a short procurement playbook (one page) that describes the exception SKU, pricing tiers, and how it gets accepted into the PO. Key points:

- Exception SKU: "Cross-Region Failover (CRF)" with three capacity tiers (small/med/large) priced as a % uplift on committed capacity.
- Rollback trigger: automatic fallback to single-region if sustained errors > 2% across 5 minutes; manual rollback within 2 hours allowed if both parties agree.
- Credit model: we recommend a blended model — fixed credit for partial-impact minutes (first 5 mins no credit), then hourly prorated credits after 30 minutes. This keeps incentives aligned for transient events.

What I included in the playbook:
- Procurement checklist (three signoffs: procurement, engineering, finance)
- Evidence packet items (delivery timeline)
- DocuSign and internal approval flow links

Next action: David/Hannah to confirm legal language in the addendum and confirm the evidence package timing. I'm happy to iterate quickly — if Coventry can accept the playbook and the SKU approach we can embed the line and price it in the order form today.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Senior Sales Operations Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachment: OrderForm_Template_REDLINE.pdf

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Amelia Torres <amelia.torres@coventrymed.com>
Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 08:19:00 -0700
Subject: Legal redline notes — service continuity addendum

David / Ben / Amelia — quick legal summary of the redline I propose:

- Tolerance window: agree to a quarterly transient-exclusion clause described as "transient event of duration up to 120 seconds per calendar quarter, non-cumulative, not actionable for credit." This must be tied to a specific incident classification and dashboard evidence.
- Evidence delivery: initial packet within 48 hours (summary, timestamped traces, circuit topology snapshot), full incident dossier within 10 business days (root cause analysis, mitigations, and timeline).
- Order-form exception: we can accept a one-line exception but will require a minimum committed capacity for the CRF SKU and a 30-day cancellation notice for the add-on in the order form.
- Liability cap: ensure addendum references existing MSA liability cap (no standalone increase).

I attached an annotated version of the Coventry doc with inline edits. If Coventry accepts these edits we can prepare a final redline for DocuSign.

Hannah Schmitt
Counsel, Enterprise Contracts
Redwood Inference

Attachment: SLA_Evidence_Manifest.xlsx

From: Rajiv Patel <rajiv.patel@coventrymed.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Amelia Torres <amelia.torres@coventrymed.com>
Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, procurement@coventrymed.com
Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLA addendum ask — service continuity / tolerance for brief downtime

Thanks Hannah — this looks reasonable and aligns with our risk posture. Two quick clarifications before we sign off:

1) Can Redwood confirm what "timestamped traces" means in practice (sample fields and retention window)? We need to include that in our evidence checklist.
2) On the cancellation notice for CRF SKU — can custody be prorated monthly rather than 30 days flat? Procurement prefers a prorated model if usage drops.

If you can answer those two items by EOD, procurement will accept the redline and we'll kick DocuSign. Appreciate the fast turnaround from the Redwood team.

— Rajiv
Director, IT Sourcing
Coventry Medical Systems
